title: Choose the HypeCubs visual world
question: The roll dealt Waymarked Trail. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Waymarked Trail
options.lineage: UK forest-park trail maps and coloured waymarker posts
options.thesis: Every quest is a walk on a waymarked trail: coloured route discs, numbered timber posts, and a map of The Lost Forest that fills in as you move.
materials: printed trail map with contour lines
options.viewport: Home is the forest map: six creature zones, today's trail drawn in orange with three numbered posts (the creatures), and a chunky trailhead sign holding START TRAIL. Mission screens are the post you're standing at, with the move routed into the timber.
options.risk: Can tip into geography homework if drawn as a flat schematic; it has to stay chunky, illustrated and loud.

raised.raise: A small hidden Cub on every screen, waiting to be spotted. Found Cubs join My Firsts.
Rounds become an unbroken row of trail markers with a 'you are here' light moving along it. An empty row is an invitation, never a failure.
Each creature owns a map zone in its own colour (Bear Woods, Monkey Canopy, Kangaroo Meadow, Crab Shore, Flamingo Lake, Gorilla Ridge), so the whole map tells you who you've trained.

options.label: Playground Markings
options.lineage: thermoplastic markings painted on UK primary-school playgrounds
options.thesis: The app is the playground floor: hopscotch grids, number snakes and compass roses in thick primary paint on dark tarmac, the surface every 6–11 year old already plays on.
options.viewport: A hopscotch ladder runs up the screen: each square a creature level, today's quest squares glowing in yellow paint, the Cub sat on the next square. The start button is a painted target circle.
options.risk: My top pick, and the most obvious kids' world. A grey tarmac ground can feel dull unless the paint covers a lot of the screen.

options.label: Multiplane Forest Dawn
options.thesis: The Lost Forest as layered painted planes that slide past as the story moves, the campfire as the one warm light.
options.viewport: A deep forest scene in four layers; the quest card sits on the nearest plane and the camera drifts toward the campfire.
options.case: Kids love a storybook forest and it fits the story, but painted layers are heavy to make with free tools, and a moody scene is harder to read at a glance mid-exercise.
options.risk: Can look sleepy and grown-up, not energetic.

options.label: Drum Machine Step Row
options.case: Children don't recognise drum machines, and it reads as a music app.
options.kept: Rounds as one unbroken row of markers with a moving light.

options.label: Mid-century Magazine
options.case: A grown-up editorial world; kids wouldn't see themselves in it.
options.kept: A hidden mark on every screen for patient eyes to find.

options.label: Sleeping City Fold
options.case: A night-time, sleepy world works against an energetic movement app.
options.kept: Every region keeps its own colour, so the map shows who's been trained.

options.label: Deco Cinema Lobby
options.case: Glamour for grown-ups, nothing a child plays in.
options.kept: Each step forward feels like arriving somewhere new.

options.label: Algorave Floor
options.case: Neon-on-black is exactly the generic look you ruled out.
options.kept: Show what's coming next before it happens.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A bright, friendly kids' fitness app done really well: white screens, rounded cards, one strong primary colour and a mascot.
canonCard.viewport: A mascot greeting, a big start button, and a row of creature cards.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every kids' app, the generic feel you wanted to avoid.
